metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.candidate_universe: OS/browsers: Windows, macOS/iOS, Linux kernel userspace, Chrome/Chromium, Firefox. Databases: MySQL, MongoDB, PostgreSQL components. Games: Unreal Engine, Unity runtime, Source 2. Safety/latency-critical: NASA JPL Mars rovers, SpaceX Falcon 9/Dragon flight software, high-frequency trading systems (e.g. Bloomberg-adjacent HFT engineering). Tech companies: Google (Search, Chrome, core infra), Microsoft (Windows, Office), Adobe (Photoshop/Illustrator/Premiere).

component_findings.current_continuity: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--c): C++ has extensive, well-documented, multi-source production deployment evidence spanning all 6 predeclared domains: consumer OS/browsers (Windows, Chrome, Firefox), core internet infrastructure (Google Search/Chrome backend), databases (MySQL, MongoDB), AAA game engines (Unreal Engine), safety-critical aerospace (NASA JPL Mars rovers, SpaceX Falcon 9/Dragon flight software confirmed directly by SpaceX engineers), and finance/HFT and embedded/automotive systems. metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.limitations: TIOBE-style popularity/search-share figures and generic 'companies that use X' listicles are used only as corroborating context, not as the sole proxy, consistent with methodology restrictions on standalone popularity proxies.
metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.selection_rule: Use public, independently checkable production evidence; named deployments must be documented by the deploying organization or corroborated by credible independent sources. Popularity surveys alone do not prove deployment.

metric.third_party_tool_availability.candidate_universe: CMake/Meson/Bazel (build); vcpkg/Conan/Hunter/Spack (package managers); clang-tidy/cppcheck/PVS-Studio/Coverity/SonarSource (static analysis); clang-format (formatting); gdb/lldb/Visual Studio debugger (debugging); CLion/Visual Studio/VS Code+clangd (IDE); Valgrind/perf/Google Sanitizers/Intel VTune (profiling/dynamic analysis); GitHub Actions+SBOM generators for Conan/vcpkg (CI/security).

component_findings.build_test_coverage: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--c): C++ has mature, actively maintained, multi-vendor tooling covering all 8 predeclared categories (build, package management, static analysis, formatting, debugging, IDE integration, profiling, CI/SBOM), each with more than one credible option and first-party or near-first-party vendor backing (Microsoft/vcpkg, JFrog/Conan, LLVM/clang-tooling, JetBrains/CLion). This is near-ceiling tool availability; the score is not 100 because C++ lacks a single official/standard package manager and a meaningful share of the ecosystem historically manages dependencies manually, per the cited academic study and survey, which is treated as a mild availability/uniformity deduction rather than absence of tooling
component_findings.ci_devops: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--c): CLion adds native vcpkg support and bundles Clang-Tidy/Clang analyzer integration; Visual Studio and VS Code (via clangd) provide additional first-party and community integrations.

component_findings.editor_ide: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--c): Fixed, language-neutral checklist of 8 third-party tool categories every systems/application language is checked against: (1) build system, (2) dependency/package manager, (3) static analyzer/linter, (4) code formatter, (5) debugger, (6) IDE/editor integration, (7) profiler/dynamic analysis, (8) CI/build-service and SBOM/security tooling. For each category the target is the tool most frequently named as the de-facto standard by independent, language-neutral sources (official docs, JetBrains ecosystem survey, GitHub topic co-occurrence, academic ecosystem study) identified before scoring began. This rule and depth are applied identically across all 10 languages in this evaluation.

metric.third_party_tool_availability.limitations: Popularity/usage figures (e.g. 80% Conan+vcpkg share, one-third no-tooling rate) are used only as declared supporting evidence alongside qualitative tool-category coverage, not as a standalone proxy, per methodology.
metric.third_party_tool_availability.selection_rule: Inspect the same fixed tool categories for every language and require independently maintained current tools; official first-party tools may be cited only as context, not as third-party availability.
